items.stem: What does a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) primarily provide?

options.text: An inventory of the components and dependencies that make up the software
options.rationale: Correct: an SBOM lists components so you can answer 'are we affected?' quickly.

options.text: A guarantee that the software has no vulnerabilities
options.rationale: An SBOM lists components; it does not certify them vulnerability-free.

options.text: The source code of every dependency
options.rationale: An SBOM is an inventory, not the code itself.

options.text: A signed legal contract with each vendor
options.rationale: It is a technical inventory, not a contract.

items.explanation: Correct: an SBOM lists components so you can answer 'are we affected?' quickly.

items.stem: Which two practices reduce the risk of pulling a malicious or unexpected dependency version? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: pinning prevents unexpected version changes between builds.
Correct: signature verification confirms the artifact's origin and integrity.
Floating tags invite unexpected and potentially malicious updates.

options.text: Disabling all dependency scanning to speed builds
options.rationale: Disabling scanning removes a key safeguard.

items.explanation: Correct: pinning prevents unexpected version changes between builds.; Correct: signature verification confirms the artifact's origin and integrity.

items.stem: A dependency is cryptographically signed and the signature verifies. What does this establish?

options.text: That the artifact came from the expected signer and was not altered in transit
options.rationale: Correct: signing proves origin and integrity, not absence of vulnerabilities.

options.text: That the dependency contains no security vulnerabilities
options.rationale: A valid signature says nothing about vulnerabilities in the code.

options.text: That the dependency has an open-source license
That the dependency will never need updating
options.rationale: Signed code still needs updates and scanning.

items.explanation: Correct: signing proves origin and integrity, not absence of vulnerabilities.
